title: Change management versus change control
blurb: Never mix them up again: change management moves the organization to its target state; change control protects the project baseline.
question: On a repairs-app project, tenants must be helped to stop phoning and start booking online, and the senior user wants a new feature added to the approved design. Which is change management and which is change control?

teach.body: Change management is the means by which an organization transitions from its current state to its target state (people element). Change control is the procedure that ensures changes to the project baseline are identified, assessed and then approved, rejected or deferred (issues practice). In plain English: change management moves people to a new way of working; change control decides whether an agreed product may be altered.

rows.label: Question it answers
values: How do we get people there?

teach.body: A change is a modification to an approved product in the baseline. The project baseline is the current approved versions of management and project products subject to change control. A request for change proposes a change to a baseline; an off-specification is a product that will not meet its specification. The project board is the ultimate authority but may delegate to a change authority, ideally with a change budget. A concession accepts an off-specification without corrective action.

teach.h: How change control works: the issues technique

steps.label: Assess
steps.sub: impact on baseline, targets, business case

steps.label: Decide
steps.sub: approve, reject, or ask for more

teach.caption: Steps 1 to 3 usually by the PM with support; decisions by the board, a change authority or the PM within delegated authority (manual 10.3.1).

head: 6th edition (2017)
PRINCE2 7
teach.caption: In PRINCE2 7, issue management encompasses change control.

root.label: Does it alter an approved product in the baseline?

children.label: Is it about people moving to new ways of working?

teach.body: Wrenfield Homes is replacing phone-booked repairs with an app. Project manager Hannah Ellis's change management approach describes the current state (phone queues), an interim state (app and phone side by side) and the target state (most repairs booked online), with tenant drop-in sessions and a help line. Separately, senior user Callum Reid asks to add photo upload to the approved product description: Hannah captures it as a request for change, assesses its impact and passes it to the change authority.

teach.text: Classic exam trap: 'change management' in PRINCE2 7 is NOT change control. Requests for change, off-specifications, change authority and the change budget all belong to the issues practice and the issue management approach, not to the change management approach.

items: Change management: organizational transition from current to target state (people element, change management approach).
Change control: identify, assess and approve, reject or defer changes to the baseline (issues practice).
The issue management approach describes how changes to the baseline are assessed and controlled.
The board is the ultimate authority for changes but may delegate to a change authority with a change budget.
The 6th edition 'change' theme is now the issues practice; the change control approach is now the issue management approach.

summary: You can now separate change management (moving the organization from current to target state, set out in the change management approach) from change control (deciding on changes to the project baseline through the issues practice and the issue management approach). You can also use the change control vocabulary correctly.

A.q: In PRINCE2 7, which practice is responsible for change control?
A.why: The issues practice collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the project's baseline; in PRINCE2 7 issue management encompasses change control.

whyNot.0: The progress practice compares actual achievements with plans, forecasts and controls deviations; it does not control changes to the baseline.
whyNot.1: The quality practice defines and checks requirements; changes to approved products go through the issues practice.
whyNot.3: The organizing practice defines the structure of accountability and responsibilities.

options: The means by which an organization moves from its current state to its target state
The procedure ensuring baseline changes are identified, assessed, then decided on
The plan for consultation, trials, training and a help line during the transition
The set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices within the project team
A.why: Change control is the procedure that ensures changes to the project baseline are identified, assessed and then approved, rejected or deferred (manual 10.2.3).

whyNot.0: That is change management, part of the people element.
whyNot.2: Those are enabling activities in the change management approach.
whyNot.3: That is the definition of culture.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 7, how changes to the project baseline will be assessed and controlled is described in the [?] management approach.
A.why: The issue management approach describes how issues are captured and reported and how changes to the baseline are assessed and controlled. It replaced the old change control approach.

whyNot.1: The change management approach covers organizational transition to the target state, not baseline control.
whyNot.2: There is no configuration management approach among the nine; configuration control is covered within the issue management approach.
whyNot.3: The quality management approach covers quality techniques, standards and responsibilities.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Change management is part of the people element.
2. Change control is part of the issues practice.
3. The change management approach records each request for change.
4. The issue management approach plans enabling activities for transition.
B.why: Change management sits in the people element (1) and change control in the issues practice (2).

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: requests for change are recorded in the issue register under the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: enabling activities belong in the change management approach.
whyNot.3: Both are false: the two approaches are the other way round.

B.q: The senior user asks to add a photo-upload feature to a product whose description has already been approved. How should this be handled?
options: As an enabling activity in the change management approach
As a characteristic of the target state for the business
As a concern from a key influencer in the stakeholder analysis
As a request for change under the issues practice
B.why: A proposal to change an approved, baselined product is a request for change, handled through change control in the issues practice.

whyNot.0: Enabling activities help people through transition; they do not cover changes to approved products.
whyNot.1: Target state characteristics describe the organization after transition, not changes to a product description.
whyNot.2: The senior user holds a project role, and a proposal to alter an approved product is a request for change, not stakeholder analysis.

B.q: Which term describes the current approved versions of the management and project products that are subject to change control?
B.why: The project baseline is the current approved versions of the management products and project products that are subject to change control (manual 10.1).

whyNot.0: The target state is the organizational state the change management approach aims for.
whyNot.2: The product register records the products of a plan and their status; it is not the baseline itself.
whyNot.3: The change budget is money set aside to fund approved changes.

C.q: A housing association is replacing phone repair bookings with an app. Which pairing is correct?
options: Helping tenants book online is change control; adding a feature to the approved design is change management
Both are change control, recorded and decided through the issue register
Helping tenants book online is change management; adding a feature to the approved design is change control
Both are change management, set out in the change management approach
C.why: Moving tenants to a new way of working is organizational transition (change management); altering an approved product is a change to the baseline (change control).

whyNot.1: Supporting tenants through the transition is not a change to the baseline, so it is not change control.
whyNot.3: Altering an approved product needs change control in the issues practice, not the change management approach.

C.q: Who is the ultimate authority for requests for change and off-specifications?
C.why: The project board is the ultimate authority for requests for change and off-specifications, though it may delegate to a change authority or the project manager (manual 10.2.4).

whyNot.0: A change authority holds delegated authority within limits set by the board.
whyNot.1: The project manager may be given delegated authority, but the board remains the ultimate authority.
whyNot.2: The senior user sits on the board but is not by themselves the ultimate authority for changes.

C.q: Which is NOT part of change control in PRINCE2 7?
options: Assessing a request for change against the baseline
Granting a concession for an off-specification
Funding an approved change from the change budget
Planning training before the move to the target state
C.why: Planning training before transition is an enabling activity in the change management approach (people element), not change control.

whyNot.0: Assessing requests for change against the baseline is a core part of change control.
whyNot.1: A concession is a decision on an off-specification, made through change control.
whyNot.2: The change budget funds approved changes, a change control mechanism.

reteach.title: The kitchen refit
reteach.question: During a kitchen refit, which is about getting the family used to the new kitchen, and which is about altering the agreed design?

blocks.body: Showing the family how the new induction hob works, and cooking with them in the first week, is change management: helping people move to a new way of living. Asking the fitter to swap the agreed sink for a bigger one is change control: a proposed change to an approved design, assessed for cost and time and approved or rejected by whoever holds the budget.

blocks.text: If it alters something already approved in the baseline, it is change control. If it moves people to a new way of working, it is change management.

explain.body: Change management is organizational transition from the current state to the target state, through any interim states. It is planned in the change management approach, part of the people element.

test.q: Which management product sets out how the organization will move from its current state to its target state?
test.why: The change management approach establishes the target organizational state and how the business will move there from the current state.

whyNot.1: The issue management approach covers issues and control of baseline changes.
whyNot.2: The benefits management approach covers achieving outcomes and confirming benefits.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach covers the means and frequency of communication and feedback.

explain.body: Project baseline, change, request for change, off-specification, concession, change authority and change budget are all issues-practice terms. The change budget funds approved changes, usually alongside delegated change authority.

options: Money set aside to fund risk responses
Money set aside to fund approved changes
Money set aside for training in transition
Money held by the business for exceptions
test.why: A change budget is money (or authorized trade-offs) set aside to fund approved changes, allocated with delegated change authority.

whyNot.0: Money for risk responses is the risk budget.
whyNot.2: Training during transition is an enabling activity in change management, not what the change budget is for.
whyNot.3: Exceptions are handled through exception reports and plans, not a change budget.

explain.body: Change control runs through the issues technique: capture the issue, assess its impact, recommend options, decide (within delegated authority, or escalate) and implement the decision, updating products and the baseline.

test.q: Which is the correct order of the issues technique?
test.why: The issues technique is capture, assess, recommend, decide, implement (manual 10.3.1).

whyNot.0: Options cannot be recommended before the issue has been assessed.
whyNot.1: Identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate is the risk management technique.
whyNot.3: A decision comes after assessment and a recommendation, not before.

explain.body: The 6th edition 'change' theme became the issues practice in PRINCE2 7, and the change control approach became the issue management approach. 'Change management' now has one meaning: organizational transition.

test.q: Which statement about PRINCE2 7 terminology is correct?
options: The 6th edition change theme is now the issues practice
The change control approach is now the change management approach
The 6th edition change theme is now the people element
Change management now means control of the project baseline
test.why: The change theme became the issues practice, and the change control approach became the issue management approach.

whyNot.1: The change control approach became the issue management approach.
whyNot.2: The people element is new content; the change theme's role passed to the issues practice.
whyNot.3: Change management now means organizational transition; baseline control is change control.
